headline: Protein AI models now drive conformational sampling and sequence design
label: Protein Conformational Sampling And Design
summary: Benchmarks now test whether co-folding and language models hold up for ligand poses and developability, not only for structure prediction.
synthesis: Learned protein models are increasingly used as engines for generating and exploring structural and sequence diversity. AF-RW and AF-Ensemble perturb AlphaFold weights or fine-tune model ensembles to produce alternative conformations that seed molecular dynamics, while Prodigy Protein applies masked protein language models in zero-shot, stepwise directed evolution. What is new relative to single-structure prediction is that conformational and sequence landscapes are treated as the object of optimization. Companion benchmarks temper this shift: AF3, Boltz-2 and Chai-1 are evaluated prospectively on 489 Mac1-ligand complexes against DOCK3.7 docking, and FLAb2 reports that 30 AI and biophysical models poorly predict most antibody developability properties. The items differ in task, so the shared element is model-driven exploration of sequence and structure space under explicit evaluation.
